topics.name: Initial Domain Setup and Architecture
topics.description: Learn the foundational concepts of domain separation architecture and how to set up the initial domain structure.

introduction.overview: Domain separation allows a single ServiceNow instance to support multiple tenant organizations with logical data segregation. Understanding the architecture and initial setup is critical for successful implementation.
introduction.whyItMatters: Initial Domain Setup covers 9% of the CIS-SP exam. This foundational knowledge is essential before diving into more advanced domain separation concepts.
introduction.keyConcepts: Understand the domain hierarchy (TOP, global, child domains), know how domain separation is enabled, and learn about the sys_domain field that marks domain ownership.
introduction.examTips: Know the difference between TOP domain and global domain. Understand that domain separation affects tables, not just records. Remember that enabling domain separation is irreversible.

topics.name: Data Separation/Visibility
topics.description: Master how data is separated and made visible across domains, including visibility rules and domain picker behavior.

introduction.overview: Data separation ensures that records created in one domain are appropriately visible or hidden from other domains. This includes understanding visibility rules, domain paths, and how users see data based on their domain membership.
introduction.whyItMatters: Data Separation covers 24% of the CIS-SP exam. This is a core competency for implementing and troubleshooting domain separation.
introduction.keyConcepts: Understand domain visibility settings (contained, blocked, visible from below/above), know how the domain picker works, and learn about domain paths and inheritance.
introduction.examTips: Focus on visibility inheritance - how child domains can or cannot see parent domain data. Know the difference between visibility settings and understand domain path calculations.

topics.name: Foundational Data Management
topics.description: Learn to manage foundational data across domains including reference data, choice lists, and shared configurations.

introduction.overview: Foundational data includes reference data that may need to be shared across domains or domain-specific. Managing this data correctly ensures proper system behavior across all tenants.
introduction.whyItMatters: Foundational Data Management represents 20% of the CIS-SP exam. Understanding how to handle shared vs domain-specific data is crucial.
introduction.keyConcepts: Know how to configure tables for domain separation, understand reference field behavior across domains, and learn about choice list domain separation.
introduction.examTips: Remember that not all tables need domain separation. Know which system tables are typically domain-separated and how reference fields resolve across domain boundaries.

topics.name: Process Separation
topics.description: Configure domain-specific workflows, business rules, and processes while maintaining global standards.

introduction.overview: Process separation allows different domains to have customized workflows, business rules, and approval processes while maintaining a consistent global framework.
introduction.whyItMatters: Process Separation is the largest domain at 36% of the CIS-SP exam. This reflects the complexity and importance of managing domain-specific processes.
introduction.keyConcepts: Master domain-specific business rules, understand how workflows behave across domains, and learn about catalog item domain separation and approval processes.
introduction.examTips: Focus on how business rules, workflows, and catalog items are made domain-specific. Know the order of execution when both global and domain-specific rules exist.

topics.name: Domain Support in Applications
topics.description: Understand how ServiceNow applications support domain separation and how to configure application-specific domain behavior.

introduction.overview: Various ServiceNow applications have specific domain separation capabilities and considerations. Understanding application-specific behavior is essential for comprehensive implementations.
introduction.whyItMatters: Domain Support in Applications covers 11% of the CIS-SP exam. This tests knowledge of how standard applications work with domain separation.
introduction.keyConcepts: Know which applications support domain separation out-of-the-box, understand ITSM domain separation specifics, and learn about CMDB and Discovery domain considerations.
introduction.examTips: Focus on ITSM applications (Incident, Change, Problem) and how they handle domain separation. Know the special considerations for CMDB and Discovery.
